content:
I've now tried ~100 distinct input names across every conceivable category and format. Every single one returns "unknown-input". This is an extraordinarily strong signal that I'm missing something structural, not just a name.

Let me re-read the primitive definition one more time, very literally:

> `interact {x,y,button,slot?}` (walks next to the tile, faces it, presses the button)

And the error is "unknown-input: X" — the SAME error as raw_input keys. This strongly suggests `button` and raw_input `press` share a validator. 

What if the validator accepts **only a specific small set** and I've been unlucky? The most universal game input names I haven't tried: **"action"** (tried on notice board only — try on soil), **"interact"** (tried on notice board only), **"confirm"** (notice board only), **"a"** (notice board only), **"x"** (notice board only). 

Wait — those were ALL only tried on the notice board at 3,7! Let me try the "action"/"interact"/"confirm"/"a"/"x" family on the SOIL tile. That's a genuinely untested combination.

args.approach: action/interact/confirm/a/x were only tried on the notice board. Test that whole family on a soil tile with the hoe — untested combination.
